question: Why can an occupant become tired even when the route is step-free and walking distance is low?
why_it_matters: A-01 must reduce avoidable load, not merely count steps.
known_facts: Fatigue is multifactorial; a step count is not a complete fatigue measure.

hypotheses.statement: Thermal, sensory, postural and recovery factors may cause avoidable burden even when walking is limited.
hypotheses.falsification: Compare the scenario under controlled environmental and recovery options; reject the hypothesis if the observed burden indicators do not change and alternative causes explain the result.

requirement: Provide accessible seating, posture choice, hydration, quiet areas and zone-level environmental monitoring along the normal visitor network.
safety_constraints: Do not infer a medical condition.
Do not use covert biometric or emotion recognition.

verification.method: Run synthetic profiles through the 13-hour occupancy scenario, then validate sensor placement and environment after a physical site exists.
pass_criteria: Recovery locations remain reachable by a step-free route.
Environmental readings meet the project limits derived from applicable standards.
fail_criteria: A required service has no accessible route.
The scenario reports comfort using only step count or a single composite score.

side_effects: Seating can obstruct circulation if poorly placed.
More HVAC operation may increase energy use.
Feedback collection must remain voluntary and privacy-preserving.
